exposure: cooled radiofrequency ablation (CRF) of the trochanteric branch of the femoral nerve
cohort: Eight patients suffering from Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome (GTPS) underwent cooled radiofrequency ablation (CRF) of the trochanteric branch of the femoral nerve.
finding: Cooled radiofrequency ablation (CRF) of the nervus femoralis to the trochanter was found to be safe and effective in providing long-term pain relief for patients with Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome (GTPS).
